questions.text: What role does a reducer play in an explicit agent state graph?

options.A: It decides the model’s next generated token from vocabulary logits.
options.B: It automatically grants approval for every side-effecting tool call.
options.C: It specifies how an incoming field update combines with that field’s existing state.
options.D: It deletes all checkpoints after every successful node execution.

questions.explanation: A reducer defines how updates merge into existing state, such as appending a list or replacing a value.

questions.text: A graph proposes a refund that requires human authorization. Where should an approval interrupt occur?

options.A: After the refund tool executes, so the reviewer can inspect the payment receipt.
options.B: Before the side-effecting refund tool runs, with the proposal preserved for review.
options.C: Only after the final answer is sent, so the user sees no delay.
options.D: At an unrelated logging node, while refund execution continues independently.

questions.explanation: Approval must gate the side effect before execution; persisting the proposal allows review and a controlled resume.

questions.text: The lesson router returns "tools" if getattr(last, "tool_calls", None) is truthy, otherwise END. If the last message has tool_calls=[], where does it route?

options.A: END, because an empty list is falsey.
options.C: Both branches, because an empty list means parallel dispatch.
options.D: It raises AttributeError because getattr cannot return lists.

questions.explanation: The condition tests truthiness, not attribute existence. An empty list is falsey, so the router returns END.
